indemnity: A promise to cover the other side's losses if something goes wrong.
indemnification: A promise to cover the other side's losses if something goes wrong.
liquidated damages: A fixed amount agreed in advance as compensation for a breach.
force majeure: Events beyond anyone's control (like natural disasters) that may excuse non-performance.
non-compete: A restriction on working for competitors or starting a competing business after this agreement ends.
non-solicitation: A restriction on contacting or hiring the other side's employees or clients.
arbitration: A way to resolve disputes privately instead of going to court.
jurisdiction: The court or legal system that will handle disputes under this agreement.
governing law: The country's or state's laws that apply to this agreement.
termination: Ending the agreement before its natural expiry.
lock-in period: A minimum time you must stay in the agreement before you can leave.
notice period: The time you must give in advance before ending the agreement or making a change.
security deposit: Money paid up front as a guarantee, usually returned when the agreement ends.
earnest money: A deposit showing you are serious about a deal; may be lost if you back out.
escrow: Money held by a third party until conditions are met.
lien: A legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.
warranty: A promise that something is true or will work as described.
representation: A statement of fact made to persuade the other side to enter the agreement.
covenant: A binding promise to do or not do something.
waiver: Giving up a right or claim voluntarily.
assignment: Transferring your rights or duties under this agreement to someone else.
subcontracting: Hiring someone else to do part of your work under this agreement.
confidentiality: A duty to keep certain information secret.
intellectual property: Creations of the mind — inventions, designs, brand names, artistic works, software.
IP assignment: Transferring ownership of intellectual property to someone else.
work product: Anything you create as part of your work under this agreement.
service bond: A requirement to work for a minimum period or repay training costs.
probation: A trial period at the start of employment.
variable pay: Part of your salary that depends on performance or company results.
gratuity: A lump-sum payment made to employees after completing a minimum period of service.
provident fund: A retirement savings scheme where both employer and employee contribute.
stamp duty: A tax paid to the government to make certain documents legally valid.
registration: Recording a document with a government office to make it legally enforceable.
leave and licence: A type of rental agreement common in India where the owner gives permission to use the property.
licensor: The person who owns the property and grants permission to use it.
licensee: The person who receives permission to use someone else's property.
lessor: The landlord or property owner in a lease agreement.
lessee: The tenant or renter in a lease agreement.
encumbrance: A claim or restriction on a property, such as a mortgage or lien.
foreclosure: A legal process where a lender takes property when a borrower fails to repay.
collateral: Property or assets offered as security for a loan.
hypothecation: Pledging an asset as security without giving up possession.
EMI: Equated Monthly Instalment — a fixed monthly payment on a loan.
moratorium: A temporary pause on payments or obligations.
sui generis: Unique; of its own kind — used for special legal categories.
pro rata: In proportion — for example, rent for part of a month.
mutatis mutandis: With the necessary changes — applying a rule to a new situation.
prima facie: At first sight — something that appears true unless disproved.
ad hoc: For a specific purpose; not planned in advance.
pari passu: On equal footing; at the same rate.
verbatim: Word for word; exactly as written.
